content:
shan: heads up — we saw a ~25% perf regression on long-context (seq=4096) requests routed to A100 pools after yesterday's kernel tweak. latency spike starts at token ~6000 in traces.

mei: which kernel path is it picking? tensorcore or generic?

shan: generic. profiler shows we fell back to matmul_no_tc for several attention layers. suspecting our FP8/TC capability detection flipped. paste from probe run:
```
[hw-probe] sm: 80
[hw-probe] has_tensor_cores: true
[hw-probe] supports_bf16: true
[hw-probe] supports_fp8: false
[decision] selected_kernel: matmul_no_tc (reason: fp8 capability missing)
```

alex: hmm — A100 should support TC BF16 but not FP8 natively. we used to route A100->tc_matmul when bf16 present even if fp8 absent. did the last change tighten the condition to require FP8?

shan: yes, change in 1783ccf tightened it: we require CAP_FP8 for all tc paths to avoid correctness issues with quantized kernels. that made routing stricter.

sanjay: that explains the regression. for long seq the TC kernel gives 2.5x throughput. we should either revert or add sequence-length-aware gating: for seq>1024 prefer tc_matmul when bf16==true even if fp8==false.

mei: agree on seq-gating. also we saw KV cache memory layout differs between the two kernels which affects cache hit behavior. need to verify correctness if we force tc path without fp8.

alex: suggestion: introduce a tolerant-detection flag and runtime override. quick patch: allow TC if (has_tensor_cores && supports_bf16) && (force_tc_by_seqlen || supports_fp8)

shan: prototype patch worked on my dev box. perf table: 
```
route              | p99 latency | throughput
matmul_no_tc       | 120ms       | 10 tok/s
tc_matmul (bf16)   | 48ms        | 26 tok/s
```

mei: nice. what about safety? any numerical diffs? run evals on our quality prompts.

shan: ran diff on 200 prompts. mean edit-distance 0.0006, max 0.002. looks fine but need broader eval.

sanjay: can we add an env var to force kernel to test fleet canary? REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=tc_matmul or REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=seqlen:>=1024->tc

alex: infra-bot can you create a canary job and a CI perf test for seqlen=2048/4096?

infra-bot: created canary run #canary-592 on dedicated-a100-pool. CI perf job added as redwood/eng-runtime:kernel-routing/seqlen-regress. Results will land in ~2 hours.

mei: also add a probe improvement: device capability should prefer driver-reported bits but fall back to heuristic if driver is known-buggy. e.g. if driver_version >= 520 and sm>=80 and bf16==true then assume tensorcore-bf16 path safe.

alex: implement as small table in hw_probe: 
```json
{
  "workarounds": [
    {"driver_regex": "^520\\.", "sm_min": 80, "assume_fp8": false, "allow_tc_without_fp8": true}
  ]
}
```

shan: sounds good. final action items:
- alex: add runtime env override + seqlen gating (PR expected today)
- mei: expand eval suite to 5k prompts and check numeric regression thresholds
- shan: run perf canary and KV-cache correctness tests on canary-592
- sanjay: monitor metrics and rollback policy if error rate or quality regressions > threshold

sanjay: thumbs up. if canary looks good we'll roll to dedicated pools tomorrow. :thumbsup:

shan: cool — thanks all. I'll attach perf flamegraphs and the exact probe logs to the PR.
